seoTitle: AlamarBlue Cell Viability / Percent Reduction Calculator
seoDesc: AlamarBlue (resazurin) is reduced by living cells to resorufin, which is fluorescent and pink. Free alamarblue cell viability / percent reduction calculator:
h1: AlamarBlue Cell Viability / Percent Reduction Calculator
summary:
AlamarBlue (resazurin) is reduced by living cells to resorufin, which is fluorescent and pink. It returns percent reduction, viability relative to control and cytotoxicity, and the panel shows all of them at once.

Viability is the reduction relative to a control, corrected for the background of medium alone. This calculator does that three-point correction. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the AlamarBlue Cell Viability / Percent Reduction
sections.html:
Viability (%) = (sample − blank) ÷ (control − blank) × 100

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
samplefluorescence of treated wellsRFU
controlfluorescence of untreated wellsRFU
blankmedium plus reagent, no cellsRFU

Where the relationship comes from. AlamarBlue/resazurin reduction chemistry; 70% viability threshold from ISO 10993-5.

sections.title: How do I use the AlamarBlue Cell Viability / Percent Reduction?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: sample fluorescence of 32,000 RFU, control fluorescence of 48,000 RFU, medium-only blank of 2,500 RFU.

Substituting them into the formula gives percent reduction of 64.84%, viability relative to control of 64.84%, cytotoxicity of 35.16%.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
above 90%Non-cytotoxicwithin normal variation
70 – 90%Mildwatch for dose-dependent effects
below 70%Cytotoxicthe usual threshold in ISO 10993 testing

  • AlamarBlue measures metabolic activity, not cell number. A cytostatic compound lowers the signal without killing anything.

  • The blank matters: resazurin is partly reduced by medium components, and an uncorrected blank inflates weak signals.

  • Incubation time should be identical for all wells; reduction is enzymatic and keeps going.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Reading in the wrong channel — resorufin fluoresces at 590 nm with excitation around 560 nm.
  • Comparing plates incubated for different times.
  • Leaving the reagent in the wells during imaging, where it bleaches.

faq.a: The share of the dye that the cells have reduced, corrected for the medium-only blank — the same number as viability when the control is fully viable.

faq.q: Can I use absorbance instead of fluorescence?
faq.a: Yes, at 570 nm against a 600 nm reference; the calculation is identical.

faq.q: What does the AlamarBlue Cell Viability / Percent Reduction actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns percent reduction, viability relative to control and cytotoxicity. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
